title: En el restaurante
blurbEn: Dinner out from start to bill. Everything you need to order food in Spanish, and your first look at 'querer'.
body:
Los viernes ceno en un restaurante con mis amigos.

El camarero llega a nuestra mesa con el menú.

—Buenas noches. ¿Qué quieren tomar?

—Yo quiero una ensalada y pollo con arroz, por favor —dice mi amiga Sofía.

—Para mí, pescado y una botella de agua —digo yo.

La comida llega en quince minutos y está muy buena. Después del postre pedimos la cuenta. Pagamos y volvemos a casa contentos.
translationEn:
On Fridays I have dinner in a restaurant with my friends.

The waiter arrives at our table with the menu.

"Good evening. What would you like to order?"

"I want a salad and chicken with rice, please," says my friend Sofía.

"For me, fish and a bottle of water," I say.

The food arrives in fifteen minutes and it is very good. After dessert we ask for the bill. We pay and go home happy.

quieren.note: The polite plural form, used by waiters addressing a table.

Buenas.note: 'Buenas noches' works as both hello and goodbye after dark.

phrases.note: After a preposition, 'yo' becomes 'mí'. Never 'para yo'.
'pedir' is to ask *for* something. Asking a question is 'preguntar'.
